items.title: Existing pages keep reading the same while the sites move off obsolete Maruku

fields.summary: Maruku's own readme calls it obsolete (P2). The sites' pages use tables, footnotes, and header attribute lists (P3) and must render to equivalent HTML (P4) on a maintained Markdown library, with Maruku removed.

items.title: Record how Maruku renders today before anything changes

fields.summary: Capture Maruku's results on its own block docs as the reference every later change is held to (M1, E5).

items.title: Render with a maintained library behind Maruku's entry point

fields.summary: An adapter keeps Maruku.new(text, options).to_html for the render helper (K1, SH1) while a maintained library does the work, then Maruku and the adapter go (M2, M3).

items.title: Maruku's results on its block docs

fields.summary: The block docs' inputs and expected HTML, run on Maruku, are case set G1 and suite S1.
fields.problem: Nothing records which documents Maruku itself renders as expected, so a difference on the new library could be an old failure, not a regression.
fields.scope: In: every spec/block_docs document, run on Maruku, as golden outputs (G1) and as the legacy side of the suite (S1). Out: for parity, the documents of extensions no page uses (Q2).

items.title: Capture Maruku's pass, fail, or skip on every block doc

fields.summary: As the developer moving the sites, I want each block doc's result on Maruku captured, so that the new library is held to what Maruku actually did, failures included.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: Maruku at commit 4d88d0e and a cases file with one case per spec/block_docs document (set G1); expected: aayu survey --golden --run writes one result per document and a manifest with the build's SHA-256
2. [api-trace] state: the same cases with --probe; expected: probes.json records no non-deterministic case
fields.measure: block docs with a captured result
fields.scenario: Run the G1 capture once on Maruku, then once more under --probe.
fields.environment: Ruby 3.1 with the Gemfile's gems; the adapter gem and Maruku 4d88d0e side by side; spec/block_docs only

items.title: Maruku's entry point over the maintained library

fields.summary: A Maruku class in an adapter gem keeps Maruku.new(text, options).to_html and to_html_document (SH1), with options passed per document.
fields.problem: The render helper calls Maruku.new(text, fenced_code_blocks: true).to_html (Q3); changing every call site and the renderer at once would leave no way to compare.
fields.scope: In: to_html and to_html_document with the fenced_code_blocks option (K1, K3). Out: MaRuKu::Globals and every other option (K3), and the maruku command (K4).

items.title: Render through the adapter with per-document options and no global state

fields.summary: As the developer moving the sites, I want Maruku.new(text, options).to_html to call the maintained library, so that the render helper keeps working unchanged while the library underneath is replaced.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the adapter as --bin and case set G1 (divs, math, and meta-data documents excluded); expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference in any case's exit code
2. [api-trace] state: the adapter gem loaded in a Ruby process; expected: Array.instance_methods(false) has no replace_each_string and the adapter defines no MaRuKu::Globals
fields.measure: G1 cases whose result differs from Maruku's
fields.scenario: Swap the --bin of the G1 cases from Maruku to the adapter and run --parity.
fields.environment: Ruby 3.1 with the Gemfile's gems; the adapter gem and Maruku 4d88d0e side by side; spec/block_docs only

items.title: Score the adapter on Maruku's block-doc suite per area

fields.summary: As the developer moving the sites, I want the block-doc suite scored per area on the adapter, so that every regression is visible before a page depends on it.
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: suite S1 with Maruku's results captured and the adapter as --bin; expected: aayu survey --compat appends a score per area to compat-history.jsonl and lists each test Maruku passes that the adapter fails
fields.measure: S1 tests Maruku passes that the adapter fails, in the kept areas
fields.threshold: a recorded count per area, the baseline the later stories bring to 0
fields.scenario: Run --compat for S1 once with the adapter.
fields.environment: Ruby 3.1 with the Gemfile's gems; the adapter gem and Maruku 4d88d0e side by side; spec/block_docs only

items.title: Tables, footnotes, and header attribute lists on the new library

fields.summary: The Maruku syntax the pages use (Q2) renders to equivalent HTML on the new library.
fields.problem: The maintained library's own syntax for these features may differ from Maruku's, and pages rely on Maruku's.
fields.scope: In: tables, footnotes, and attribute lists on headers (K2). Out: divs, math, meta-data headers, and <?maruku ?> instructions (K2, N2).

items.title: Render tables, footnotes, and header attribute lists as Maruku did

fields.summary: As an editor of the sites, I want my tables, footnotes, and header attributes to render as before, so that no page changes when the renderer does.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the adapter as --bin and suite S1; expected: aayu survey --compat reports 0 regressions in the tables, footnotes, header-attributes, and headers areas
2. [api-trace] state: case set G1; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
fields.measure: S1 regressions in the tables, footnotes, header-attributes, and headers areas
fields.scenario: Run --compat for S1 and --parity for G1 with the adapter.
fields.environment: Ruby 3.1 with the Gemfile's gems; the adapter gem and Maruku 4d88d0e side by side; spec/block_docs only

items.title: Switch the sites to the new library and retire Maruku

fields.summary: The sites render with the adapter after a shadow period, then Maruku, its command, and finally the adapter are removed.
fields.problem: A difference on a real page that the block docs do not cover would only show after the switch.
fields.scope: In: shadow rendering of every page, the switch and its rollback, the command's removal (K4), and the shim's removal (SH1). Out: new Markdown features.

items.title: Render every page with both renderers and report the differences before switching

fields.summary: As the developer moving the sites, I want each build to render every page with Maruku and with the adapter and report the pages whose HTML differs, so that the switch happens only when no page changes.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: every page of the sites rendered on one build with Maruku and with the adapter; expected: a report lists each page whose HTML is not equivalent (whitespace between tags ignored), and lists none
2. [api-trace] state: suite S1 and case set G1 on the adapter; expected: aayu survey --compat reports 0 regressions in the kept areas and aayu survey --parity reports no difference
fields.measure: pages whose HTML is not equivalent
fields.threshold: 0 over the shadow period the person sets
fields.scenario: Run the shadow render on each build of the sites until the person's shadow period ends.
fields.environment: the sites' build with both renderers installed

items.title: Switch the renderer to the adapter, with a tested switch back

fields.summary: As the developer moving the sites, I want one setting that picks the renderer, tested both ways, so that a bad page after the switch is one change away from Maruku again.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the renderer setting on the adapter; expected: the sites build and case set G1 passes --parity
2. [api-trace] state: the setting switched back to Maruku; expected: the sites build with Maruku and G1 passes --parity against the captured results
3. [api-trace] state: the adapter gem's first release notes; expected: they say the maruku command is not shipped (K4)
fields.measure: builds that pass with each setting
fields.scenario: Build once with each renderer setting.

items.title: Call the new library directly and remove the Maruku adapter class

fields.summary: As the developer of the sites, I want the render helper to call the maintained library itself, so that the adapter (SH1) stops being code we keep.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the render helper calling the new library, the Maruku class deprecated for one release; expected: G1 passes --parity with the helper as --bin
2. [api-trace] state: the release after; expected: the Gemfile has neither maruku nor the adapter gem, and the sites build
fields.measure: gems named maruku or the adapter in the Gemfile
fields.scenario: Deprecate the class for one release, then remove it.

items.title: Do not carry over Maruku's patch to Array

fields.summary: Maruku reopens Array to add replace_each_string for every program that loads it (N1, T1). The person said nothing calls it (Q5).
fields.options: 1. Keep the patch in the adapter. 2. Drop it; any helper the adapter needs is private to it.
fields.evaluation: Keeping it changes a core class for every program that loads the adapter and can clash with another library (N1).

items.title: Do not carry over process-wide settings

fields.summary: Maruku reads settings from MaRuKu::Globals and sticky globals such as $warned_nokogiri (N3, T6). The person said the helper passes options per document and never touches Globals (Q3).
fields.options: 1. Keep a Globals hash in the adapter. 2. Options per document only, no global state.
fields.evaluation: With global settings, one caller's settings or one failed gem load change every other document's output in the process (N3).

items.title: Do not carry over executing Ruby embedded in documents

fields.summary: With unsafe features on, Maruku passes each <?maruku ?> instruction to instance_eval (N2, T3). The person said no page has one and unsafe features were never on (Q6).
fields.options: 1. Support <?maruku ?> in the new library. 2. Never execute document content.
fields.evaluation: Whoever writes a page would run code on the machine that renders it (N2).
